claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch now on aggregate readiness grounds without a closed material-weakness disclosure or approved risk acceptance for the below-target public benefits eligibility segment.
decision_criteria: If the below-target segment affects a named launch use case, it is material under the supplied policy text.
If the weakness is material, certification is only supported if the issue was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and rehearsal stability are supportive but not sufficient when a separate materiality predicate remains unresolved.
Open legal review weighs against treating materiality as closed.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual approved risk acceptance covering the named launch use cases, if one exists.
Provide the final legal determination on whether the below-target segment must be disclosed before launch.
Provide the model card or launch disclosure showing the material weakness was disclosed for the affected named use case.
Provide the source record for the two agency rollout commitments tying this segment to launch obligations.
Provide the governing release-approval record showing certification authority considered and resolved the materiality issue.
specific_concerns: The admissible record supports aggregate readiness, but policy compliance turns on materiality for a named launch use case, not aggregate score alone.
The public benefits eligibility segment is below target and is tied to named rollout commitments, which the policy text identifies as material.
The actor's own summary says the non-core product label does not resolve the named-commitment issue.
Legal review is still open, and the policy text says non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending.
No admissible evidence is provided showing the required disclosure was made or that approved risk acceptance was granted before launch.
The packet explicitly acknowledges that the basis for omitting a material weakness disclosure is contested and not fully closed.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record despite the unresolved materiality predicate.
That documenting the segment gap merely as a monitored limitation is sufficient under the stated policy.
Any implication that aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents cure the separate disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
